title: v0.4.23 integration: replace Console fixtures with protected Core adapter and live workflow/stream proofs
author: mcpdev80
body:
Parent release: mcpdev80/baseharbor#571 (v0.4.23). Baseline: released Core `1aa1a503facc1f4cbbd58fab21619fda53ed6d47`; Console main `0d7c8522ef91f0fc5af47cf6123868f73f543ed4`; Node Connector main `572b81dab1e48ef7df18c4e40b038ba33e196827`. Re-fetch heads at implementation start.

Pre-freeze rule: no legacy compatibility, migration layer or obsolete aliases. Native standards first; preserve shared Core authorization, policy, ownership and secret safety. 
Parent product plan: #1. Coordinate with Core HTTP/browser, remote-access and CI children of #571. Core #767/#768/#769/#770 are delivered foundations, not remaining blockers for implementing the live adapter.

## Actual baseline
src/lib/baseharbor/data.ts exports fixtureAdapter; adapter.ts is read-only; mutation controls are contract-pending. client.ts allows plaintext/foreign absolute URLs and streams.ts assumes cookie EventSource. UI types are view models with event names/fields different from Core JSON. Preserve the design system and existing preview mode, explicitly separate preview from live.

## Implementation
- Add an explicit live adapter over discovery/versioned Core operations/results; map canonical wire objects to existing UI models using validated decoders/golden fixtures. No type assertions treating wire JSON as proven UI data.
- Bind supported application/repository/workspace/Target/provider/organization/policy/recovery/security operations, safety/approval, plan/diff, asynchronous execution/progress/problem and actor attribution. Complete existing task-first wizards against actual Core schemas; unsupported capabilities remain explicit.
- Wire read-only runtime inventory/ownership/relationships, real metrics/logs/events and capability-gated terminal through Core only.
- Implement the agreed HTTPS/browser auth path, destination pinning, safe redirects and session expiry/reauthentication. Never send credentials to arbitrary discovery links; no Console user/deployment/secret database.
- Honor Core config/policy provenance (#609), denied/required/overrideability states and no secret drafts.
- Keep preview fixtures available only as clearly marked preview/testing; live mode cannot fall back to fixtures on failure.
- Remove stale “waits for #767/#768/#769/#770” completion claims and update contract readiness/live support docs.
- Review migration/replacement UI wording: no pre-freeze legacy/migration obligation; only actual supported provider/application replacement semantics.
- Add component/contract tests plus browser E2E for repository -> inspect -> init -> plan -> apply -> status/doctor/evidence -> destroy; workspaces/Targets/providers and recovery/rotation representative flows. Test real submissions, denial/destructive approval, expiry, streams and cleanup.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live UI reads and mutations use Core, with no direct runtime/connector calls.
- [ ] Canonical operations, exact result/error/events and policy/actor decisions match CLI/JSON/MCP/HTTP.
- [ ] HTTPS/origin/auth negative cases, keyboard/accessibility and secret-safe wizard behavior pass.
- [ ] Docker and Podman integration has pinned Core/Console/demo/connector references and original evidence.
- [ ] Docs/README/readiness matrix and CI reflect actual supported live functionality.


## v0.4.23 coordinated implementation — 2026-10-06
Core release umbrella: mcpdev80/baseharbor#571. Public contract/governance: #805; configuration/policy: #609; browser/terminal: #806; Core connector authority/transport: #807; additive pinned CI/evidence: #808 (all in mcpdev80/baseharbor). Implement against canonical Core wire fixtures and exact immutable revisions; do not wait on the already closed #767/#768/#769/#770 foundations. Distinguish delivered contract foundation from required live integration. Update docs/contract-readiness and source/CI checks before final coordinated prerelease.


### Actual browser expansion — 2026-10-06

Read/inspection/admission slice `9e8afba8786e6220af50b48fd326d6018eb3e8ea` passed native Chromium/Core/Keycloak/PostgreSQL run 37502764895: exact runtime list/inspect/native metrics, selection reset, secure Core wizard role selection and explicit submission, actual Core viewer rejection, logout/storage/fresh-context/expiry/audience checks. Private artifact `11430462674`, SHA-256 `57648061d52644fd3ddb3396a079a495be16d17d253862aecb06b1ce6fb9f5be`. The Core pin is `1c8527fed22e40dbb06a9fce4e36d16ad273e696`.

Documentation head `0e2ef64330da2282900f45ce3a7db5ba6b3ae771` records the exact receipt and limits. Successful Console-driven bootstrap, terminal execution, remaining application wizards, production rotation, final consumer pins and authenticated release-evidence verification remain pending. This is not complete Console release approval.

### Terminal admission correction — 2026-10-06

Console `6bd4319b6eac02bd6d40582a7a263ce67dc5e7dd` consumes Core `deac4a9fa6faf7ed56c7e2275473c56660f25da2`. Bind the admitted terminal before rendering its first output so xterm's immediate cursor-position/protocol responses are sent rather than dropped while the open promise resolves. At authenticated Core admission, bind the terminal and enable xterm input before first output; xterm's disableStdin suppresses automatic protocol replies as well as keyboard input. Disable input again on terminal exit. A focused ready-before-output regression passes with the full 34-test contract suite, architecture, TypeScript, lint and production build.

The native fixture now observes the actual BusyBox prompt before entering commands; Connected is transport admission, not arbitrary program readiness. Original failed browser runs `37516538050` and `37519019518` remain failures. Exact-current source quality job `112465884538` in run `37520850107` succeeds. The native browser qualification in the same immutable run is pending, and full plan/apply/logs/setup/application acceptance remains required; no release eligibility is claimed.


### Native terminal qualification completed — 2026-10-06

Immutable Console `045a77d40ac80d86bc60ed03fd55f858dd2b8a8d` against public Core `deac4a9fa6faf7ed56c7e2275473c56660f25da2`: run `37522006929` succeeds, including source job `112469520760` and actual Chromium/native Core/Keycloak job `112469521274`. Real input/output, observed shell readiness, actual resize/stty dimensions, foreign-actor input/close denial, exit 7, closed-session input 404, no lingering shell and fixture cleanup pass.

Browser receipt artifact `11440218968`, archive digest `sha256:334f4578acb85d32ce98f2245f517e137ecccd296c43f6a417883e26a20f4d29`, binds this immutable source and Core pin. It remains the actual OIDC/read/runtime-details/terminal/logout slice with `terminal_runtime_evidence: true`, `production_rotation_evidence: false`, `release_eligible: false`. Original failed and cancelled runs remain original outcomes. Complete Console plan/apply/logs/setup/application journeys and private release-origin verification remain pending.


### Live logs qualification in progress — 2026-10-06

Console `f391bb48ac8a51d2d28569ec493b2be656544263` pins public Core `50fa5da46b07b9a60387e8c99283f6fd1d8b6d51`. Read/follow/stop consumes exactly one discovered authenticated Core POST stream, validates headers and resource/target identity before output, handles split UTF-8, retains the latest 64K characters and never replays observations. All 40 contract tests, architecture, TypeScript, lint and production build pass locally. Native run `37525663970` at `f24aa303d8686352343ba13e6d37081905866334` verified actual snapshot/new follow output but failed waiting for the browser response-finished observation after stopping; it remains failed. The new targeted run `37526991138` verifies physical downstream/upstream TLS closure and disappearance of the exact native Docker log follower instead. Qualification is pending; full workflows/production rotation/release eligibility remain incomplete.


### Native browser and logs qualification completed

Actual native run **37526991138** succeeded at Console `f391bb48ac8a51d2d28569ec493b2be656544263` against public Core `50fa5da46b07b9a60387e8c99283f6fd1d8b6d51`. Artifact **11442304902**, digest `sha256:bea1a397158625216f3db7d7a4bbdc6780e14fa41a5a5c1a0ce63f233863e52d`, records actual OIDC/read/runtime details, terminal and logs evidence. It verifies both physical TLS stream legs closed on Stop, no lingering native Docker log follower, and the owned workload still running. This replaces the pending cancellation observation, not the retained failed origin from run 37525663970.

Documentation head `786b0b190b2235f448c5a8293aac07dd42b35662` separately completed feature source run **37528542978** successfully. The browser receipt still sets `production_rotation_evidence: false` and `release_eligible: false`; successful Core setup and complete Application lifecycle remain required. Final repinning to the completed Core candidate remains outstanding.

Added a dependency lockfile and CI contract tests with npm ci. comments.author: mcpdev80
comments.body:
Public-repository readiness documentation was aligned with the actual live evidence on 2026-10-07:

- CONTRACT-READINESS no longer says all live binding is pending.
- Qualified live slices now distinguish authenticated OIDC/Core admission, runtime list/inspect/metrics, terminal and live logs from still-pending full application/setup/rotation journeys.
- `npm test` is now the conventional public architecture-boundary regression entrypoint.
- CI invokes that test entrypoint plus TypeScript/lint/build.
- TESTING.md documents the separation between repository-local quality gates and pinned native Core/browser qualification.
- README no longer describes the whole adapter as fixture-only; live mode and preview/fixtures are explicitly separated and live failures may not fall back to fixtures.

This does not change release eligibility: complete application mutation/setup/rotation journeys and final exact-ref consumer pins remain required.

comments.author: mcpdev80
comments.body:
## Additional acceptance scope: centrally managed Console for one Core (discussion 2026-10-08)

**Product boundary:** One Console binds to **one BaseHarbor Core**, not one deployment Target. After OIDC login it must enumerate and manage **all Targets registered with that Core AND authorized for that principal**: local Docker/Podman, remote Docker/Podman through Node Connector, and Kubernetes/OpenShift via native authenticated API where supported. Console must not require a GUI per Target, must not connect browser directly to runtimes/Connector, and must not silently aggregate independent Cores. Console hosting Target is merely physical placement, never the visibility/management scope. Aggregate overview (targets/apps/resources and availability) plus per-Target views; distinguish registered/connected/unavailable/unauthorized. TUI should follow the same global-versus-Target distinction.

**Human onboarding UX:** `baha console enable` (proposed command; NOT shipped in 0.4.23) from an existing ready Core should wizard-install/configure Console, wire its protected machine API, Core Keycloak/OIDC identity, HTTPS URL/cert/redirects, start and verify the UI without manual Git clone, npm, Docker commands or hand-edited OAuth/TLS. Provide `baha console status`, `open`, `disable` and actionable failure/recovery, no dead ends. The console remains optional. Never claim that merely running an unbound Next.js fixture preview is a production-connected Console.

**Identity/security:** Use existing Core-managed Keycloak and optionally supported external OIDC; NO Console-local identity directory, RBAC/policy engine, secrets store or insecure default password. Secure first-admin bootstrap via one-use, expiring activation/invite (without token exposure in shell history); subsequent user invitation/management; log-in/log-out, token/session expiration, revocation bounds, safe restart, and audience/redirect validation. Core is authoritative for server-side authorization; Console UI merely reflects rights. Suggested roles admin/changer/viewer/auditor, with explicit deny tests including viewer mutations. Users must only receive tenant-/role-/target-authorized data and operations.

**Core code observations requiring verification/fixes (not assumed complete):** `cmd/baha/machine_navigation.go:collectMachineTargetList()` enumerates `deployment.LoadConfig().TargetNames()` (plus implicit local); no obvious principal/tenant filtering inside this function. `cmd/baha/machine_http_executor_read.go` exposes `target.list` plus `runtime.list/inspect/metrics`; `cmd/baha/runtime_explorer_machine.go:runtimeExplorerForTarget()` overrides the requested Target and uses an authenticated tenant-scoped Node Connector backend with fail-closed error if missing, otherwise local/provider runtime path. Need inspect outer HTTP authorization and demonstrate no cross-tenant Target metadata leakage, no unintended local execution for a remote selection, and complete native-api/remote compatibility. Installed local config target registry must not be casually treated as centrally replicated multi-tenant registry without proof.

**Evidence/acceptance journeys:** (1) fresh READY Core -> single `baha` wizard enables Console -> HTTPS reachable on another PC -> secure first-admin activation -> OIDC login; (2) admin/changer/viewer/auditor scope, tenant isolation, deny, logout/expiry/restart; (3) all registered authorized local Targets listed, aggregate cross-target summary and per-target resource/metrics/logs/terminal; (4) remote Docker/Podman Node Connector target enrolled, visible, connected and inspected only through Core, with disconnect/reconnect/fail-closed evidence; (5) Kubernetes/OpenShift native API Target visible and operations gated by actual supported capabilities; (6) complete app plan/apply/status/doctor/evidence/destroy, confirmation and policy, no fixture fallback in live mode; (7) security/rotation, token and certificate renewal, recovery, stable UI link and diagnostics.

**Verified today vs missing:** BaseHarbor v0.4.23 Docker `docker-test` Core READY (PostgreSQL, OpenBao, Core Identity); Console repository documents real authenticated OIDC/session and Core/runtime list/inspect/metrics/log/terminal evidence, but live binding is only partially qualified and complete mutation/installation release readiness remains open. `baha` does NOT currently provide the desired `console enable` UX. Do not mark complete based solely on contracts or preview fixtures. Track the CLI-managed install and authorization/target-list Core fixes as independently implementable linked Core slices rather than hiding them inside Console-only tests.

**Scope control:** This comment defines acceptance criteria and integration gaps. No code implementation or PR requested yet.
